C-RELEASE-PIPELINE-AUTOMATION.Summary: Automate release-train boundaries, release preparation, mandatory materials verification, and the separately approved publication handoff with repository-reproducible state plus GitHub-native operational controls.
C-RELEASE-PIPELINE-AUTOMATION.Problem: The current release preflight proves version consistency and workflow coverage, but candidate admission, exclusions, owner acceptance, README/CHANGELOG/GitHub/in-app materials, screenshot freshness, and final publication approval still rely on prose and human memory. The workflow can therefore package a tag whose release boundary or user-facing materials are incomplete, while the collecting train has no machine-readable state that a required check can enforce.

Goals.Goal: Add a versioned machine-readable train manifest containing train state, target version, product payload SHA, included user-facing and operational items, explicit not-present exclusions, owner-acceptance evidence, required checks, and materials status; validate it from a clean checkout without external API access.

Mirror the operational train into a GitHub Project with typed Train, Admission, Owner acceptance, Candidate SHA, and Release state fields, updated through an idempotent workflow or CLI rather than hand-maintained prose.

Configure a pinned Release Please CLI in manifest mode to calculate SemVer from enforced Conventional Commits, generate CHANGELOG.md, and open a release-preparation pull request; reviewed repository automation normalizes every additional Mark version surface.

Add one named release-materials command that validates the requested version across CHANGELOG.md, the top README release section, the English GitHub release-notes draft, the in-app What's New content table, and all ten source locale files.

Require the in-app sheet to contain one to four ordered items, its release URL, the shared Also line, the footer label, native copy within the existing 32/90/120-character limits, and no missing locale entry.

Require every README image reference to resolve to a tracked PNG and require a candidate-specific screenshot manifest that records the candidate version, capture command, referenced image set, and file digests.

Expose stable release/governance and release/readiness checks: ordinary pull requests validate the schema and control plane without requiring a frozen train, while freeze and tag contexts verify the exact payload-to-seal boundary, admission completeness, owner acceptance, version/material consistency, screenshot digests, and tag-to-commit identity before packaging.

Protect tag authorization with an owner-approved release-authorize Environment, restrict signing secrets to a tag-only release-signing Environment, protect GitHub publication with the existing release Environment, and protect main plus v* tags with rulesets.

After the train is Ready, create the calculated annotated release tag automatically through a purpose-specific bot only after an explicit owner-approved deployment; the owner never edits version files or creates a tag by hand.

Constraints.Constraint: The gate reads only public repository content and never reads signing credentials, private recovery data, owner documents, or machine-specific paths.
The existing six-source version/tag preflight remains authoritative; the materials gate consumes its normalized version rather than creating another version authority.

Release materials remain English-first except the in-app What's New copy, which must ship as native copy in all ten supported locales; product names and shortcuts keep the repository's localization exceptions.
The release job must fail closed before packaging when any required surface or screenshot evidence is absent, mismatched, over the layout limit, or points at a nonexistent file.
The checked-in train manifest is the deterministic gate authority; GitHub Project fields are an operational mirror and their temporary unavailability cannot make a clean checkout unverifiable.

Release Please owns version calculation, the primary package version, its manifest, and CHANGELOG generation, but is configured not to create a GitHub release or tag when the preparation pull request merges; the separately approved tag automation preserves the publication boundary.

Conventional Commits are the SemVer authority: fix produces patch, feat produces minor, and ! or BREAKING CHANGE produces major. Repository checks reject unclassified release commits and reserve feat for user-visible/product-contract additions; package files, train fields, action inputs, and the GitHub Project may reflect the computed version but may not override it.

A product payload commit cannot contain its own SHA. Freeze therefore uses a metadata-only seal commit that records payloadSha; the tag points to the seal commit and readiness proves that payloadSha is its allowed ancestor and that no product code changed in the sealing delta.
Manual workflow dispatch is build-only. Production signing and publication accept only an existing v* tag whose peeled commit is the checked-out release seal.

Production signing, updater, publication, Project-sync, and repository-administration credentials are job-scoped and separated by purpose. Untrusted pull-request code never executes with those credentials.
GitHub configuration changes must be idempotent, reviewable from source-controlled configuration, least-privilege, and applied without exposing tokens or environment secrets.
Rulesets must preserve an explicit owner recovery path and must not block the release workflow from updating the refs it legitimately owns.
Drafting and validating materials does not authorize a version bump, tag, GitHub release, store upload, Homebrew publication, or any other release action.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Do not automate owner acceptance, choose which product changes belong in a train, or infer admission from a merged commit.
Do not replace GRACE change governance, GitHub Actions, the existing tag-triggered release workflow, or the separate publication approval with a third-party deployment platform.
Do not publish the 2.6.0 draft or regenerate screenshots as part of this specification step.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A valid frozen 2.6.0 train manifest names one exact payloadSha; the freeze/seal commit changes only allowlisted release evidence, every user-facing included item has owner-acceptance evidence, every commit since 2.5.3 is classified as user-facing, operational, or not present, and release/readiness fails independently for stale SHA, a product-code sealing delta, missing acceptance, ambiguous membership, non-frozen state, or missing required evidence.

The GitHub Project exists with the contracted typed fields and an idempotent sync path; a dry-run reports the intended changes without mutation, and repeated apply produces no duplicate fields or items.

With current post-2.5.3 history containing feat commits, the pinned Release Please dry-run deterministically proposes 2.6.0 and generates its CHANGELOG section; a trusted PR-head normalization step updates all six synchronized version values plus the pinned release-preflight fixture, a second run is empty, and preparation is statically prevented from tagging or publishing.

The one-time Release Please bootstrap records 2.5.3 as the current version and an explicit history boundary despite v2.5.3 not being an ancestor of main; it neither re-releases older commits nor loses the intended v2.5.3..payload change set.
A fixture containing complete, mutually consistent 2.6.0 materials passes and emits BLOCK_RELEASE_MATERIALS_CONSISTENT with the normalized version and surface counts.

Focused negative tests independently reject a missing CHANGELOG entry, stale README heading, absent GitHub notes draft, missing in-app version, missing locale key, over-limit localized copy, wrong release URL, missing README PNG, and a screenshot digest mismatch.

The production workflow is publishable only from a pushed existing v* tag created by the approved tagger, proves peeled tag commit equals the checked-out seal, invokes release/readiness before every platform packaging action, restricts signing secrets to that tag-only path, and obtains a separate approval through the existing release Environment before creating or exposing the GitHub Release.

A Ready train exposes one release-authorize deployment that reads the computed version and seal commit without free-form inputs, requires owner approval, and uses a purpose-specific bot to create the annotated tag idempotently; approval is the explicit release instruction, while rejection or timeout creates no tag.

Repository rulesets require the selected checks on main and restrict v* tag creation while retaining the documented owner recovery path; configuration export and read-back tests prove the applied state.

Manual dispatch cannot sign or publish, no free-form event value is interpolated into shell source, workflow permissions are read-only by default and job-scoped, privileged actions are pinned to immutable commit SHAs, and published release assets cannot be overwritten by a rerun.

The 2.6.0 drafts cover only accepted and explicitly queued scope; FIX-009, FIX-010, FIX-012, LISTEN_FOR_CLOSE, multi-source workspace, FIX-013, and Windows titlebar alignment remain excluded unless separately admitted before freeze.

The release protocol documents Collecting, Frozen, Ready, Released, and Aborted transitions plus recovery from a failed release PR, stale candidate, rejected environment approval, or misconfigured GitHub control.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: npx vitest run tests/renderer/release-readiness.test.js tests/renderer/release-materials.test.js tests/renderer/whatsNew/content.test.js tests/renderer/release-preflight.test.js
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Stable train, materials, GitHub-control and release-preparation markers; deterministic negative fixtures; static workflow-order assertions; and GitHub API read-back showing the Project, Environment, and rulesets match source-controlled configuration.

Assumptions.Assumption: The current Conventional Commit history after 2.5.3 calculates the next version as 2.6.0 because feat commits require a minor bump; package, Cargo, lockfile, and Tauri versions remain at 2.5.3 until the release-preparation pull request.

README screenshot freshness is represented by a committed payload-specific manifest and SHA-256 digests rather than inferred from filesystem timestamps; the digests prove identity after visual review, not visual quality.
GitHub Projects is the operational train board, while the checked-in manifest remains the release gate's reproducible authority.

Release Please owns the reviewed preparation pull request, calculated version and CHANGELOG; a release-authorize-approved bot creates the tag, signing secrets are restricted to that tag path, and publication remains separately owner-approved.

C-RELEASE-PIPELINE-AUTOMATION.AppliedEvidence: release-please workflow 160293e8 + deterministic release gates d8f666ac; the conveyor operated releases 2.6.0, 2.6.1 and 2.7.0 (seal/re-seal chain inside the v2.6.0..v2.7.0 range).
